predecessors.name: Tây Sơn dynasty
predecessors.text: the Tây Sơn lands, taken from Saigon in 1788 to Hanoi in July 1802

predecessors.name: Nguyễn lords
predecessors.text: the southern realm of the Nguyễn lords, whose rule dates from 1558

successors.name: French Indochina
successors.text: Annam and Tonkin as French protectorates (the Treaty of Patenôtre (6 June 1884) ... creating the protectorates of Annam and Tonkin), with Cochinchina already French since 1862-1867

ledger.x: 1788: Nguyễn Ánh retakes Saigon and founds his southern state.
1794: the Nguyễn take Nha Trang and Khánh Hòa.
1796: Cliopatria extends the Nguyễn shape to Phú Yên and the highlands behind it.
1799: Qui Nhơn falls to the Nguyễn.
1800: Qui Nhơn is lost again: 'the city was quickly lost and was not regained until 1801.'
1801: the Nguyễn seize Qui Nhơn and the capital.
1802: Nguyễn Ánh is crowned Emperor Gia Long at Huế.
1802: the court is at Huế (Phú Xuân), seized in 1801; the Gia Định citadel (Saigon) was the seat from 1788.
1802: Hanoi falls and the Tây Sơn end.
1803: Cambodia becomes a Vietnamese vassal.
1827: Vietnam seizes Savannakhet and Xam Neua.
1828: the Vietnamese hold on Savannakhet and Xam Neua ends no later than the Siamese annexation of Vientiane's lands.
1832: Minh Mạng annexes Panduranga, the last Cham principality.
1833: the Lê Văn Khôi revolt takes Saigon.
1833: Siam invades Cambodia and Hà Tiên.

1834: Minh Mạng ends Cambodia's vassalage: he 'declared full suzerainty over Cambodia, which he demoted to Vietnam's 32nd province'; the Nguyen page: Minh Mạng fully annexed Cambodia and renamed it Tây Thành Province.
1834: the Siamese are driven out.
1835: Saigon is recaptured from Lê Văn Khôi's rebels: Saigon was recaptured in September 1835 (Khôi died in December 1834).
1835: Vietnam organises eastern Cambodia as Trấn Tây Province.
1839: the official name becomes Đại Nam.
1841: Siam aids the Khmer revolt against Vietnamese rule.
1847: agreement on Cambodia.
1847: Vietnam withdraws from Cambodia: 'The Vietnamese withdrew their forces from Cambodia in mid-1847 and Siam did the same in April 1848.'
1847: Cambodia is again a Vietnamese tributary, under joint suzerainty.
1858: the French landing at Đà Nẵng opens the Cochinchina campaign: In September 1858, the Franco-Spanish force invaded Đà Nẵng.
1859: the French take Saigon: The alliance captured Saigon in early 1859 (caption: 17 February 1859).
1862: the Treaty of Saigon cedes the three eastern provinces.
1862: the French occupation of Saigon becomes annexation with the treaty of June 1862.
1862: the Cochinchina campaign ends with the Treaty of Saigon of June 1862; the Đà Nẵng front is not dated by the page.
1863: Cambodia leaves Huế's suzerainty in practice when France places it under protection.
1867: the French annex the western provinces.
1883: Tonkin becomes a French protectorate.
1884: Annam becomes a French protectorate.

1884: the Nguyễn state ends as a sovereign power with the Treaty of Patenôtre of 6 June 1884; the emperors reign on as figureheads, and 'all emperors after Đồng Khánh were chosen by the French' until the Empire of Vietnam ended on 25 August 1945.

wars.name: Nguyễn Ánh's war against the Tây Sơn
wars.outcome: Nguyễn victory: Qui Nhơn 1799/1801, Phú Xuân 3 May 1801, Hanoi 20 July 1802; the Tây Sơn dynasty ended.

wars.name: Lê Văn Khôi revolt
wars.outcome: Rebels held Saigon (reduced to the citadel by late 1833) until it was recaptured in September 1835; Khôi died in December 1834.

wars.name: Siamese-Vietnamese War (1833-1834)
wars.outcome: Vietnamese victory; Siam withdrew by April 1834 and Trấn Tây Province was set up in November 1835.

wars.name: Siamese-Vietnamese War (1841-1845)
wars.outcome: Stalemate: agreement of January 1847, Cambodia under joint suzerainty; both armies left in 1847-1848.

wars.name: Cochinchina campaign
wars.outcome: French victory: Saigon taken 17 February 1859; Treaty of Saigon, June 1862, cedes Gia Định, Mỹ Tho and Biên Hòa.

wars.name: French conquest of Tonkin and Annam
wars.outcome: Protectorates: Harmand Convention (1883) and Treaty of Patenôtre (6 June 1884); the Sino-French War ended with the Treaty of Tientsin of 9 June 1885.

certainty.note: A conquest state in the south and a country whose highland, Lao and Cambodian frontiers were approximate; the Chinese frontier is the Qing tributary frontier.
The Cochinchina frontier follows the provinces named in the treaties of 1862 and 1867; the highland, Lao and Chinese frontiers stay soft.
